title: The Gruesome Blood Eagle: Fact or Fiction?
hook: Did Vikings really carve enemy ribs into eagle wings, or was it a literary myth?

scenes.text: In Norse sagas, the most terrifying punishment mentioned is the 'Blood Eagle'—an agonizing execution allegedly inflicted on bitter enemies.

scenes.text: According to late Icelandic poems, the victim's spine was split open, ribs pried outward like wings, and lungs pulled out into salt.

scenes.text: Victims supposedly included King Aella of Northumbria and Halfdan Long-Leg, sacrificed directly to Odin as vengeance.
